stem: A resident pharmacy will close in 20 days. Which timing and transfer statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Delay patient-file transfers until all controlled stock is disposed of.
Send the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closure.
Identify patients served in the preceding 90 days and attempt notice at least 14 days before closure.
Handle requested file transfers promptly enough to avoid delaying therapy.
Within 14 days after closure, submit original credentials and the controlled-substance disposition attestation.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Send the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closure. Identify patients served in the preceding 90 days and attempt notice at least 14 days before closure. Handle requested file transfers promptly enough to avoid delaying therapy. Within 14 days after closure, submit original credentials and the controlled-substance disposition attestation.

choice_analysis.D: Supported: Handle requested file transfers promptly enough to avoid delaying therapy.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Within 14 days after closure, submit original credentials and the controlled-substance disposition attestation.

related_facts: A resident pharmacy generally must give the Board written certified-mail notice at least 14 days before intended closure and provide the required closure and controlled-substance information.
A closing pharmacy identifies patients served in the preceding 90 days, attempts notice at least 14 days before closure, posts conspicuous notice, and supports timely patient-file transfer.
